people.name: Mike Brooks
people.fit_reason: Surname in slug; RETIRED 2024 Feb 29; disqualified as prospect

needs_review.finding: Jacqueline Huggins, Carol Pebley, Joyce Wood, Lauren Denny, Scott Rayl each appear as single-name records on pages. Wycliffe states some missionaries withhold details for security.
needs_review.evidence: Personal pages /partner/E5B4E7, /partner/EFCF8F, /partner/45D467, /partner/servantlibrarian, /partner/scottrayl show specialist roles (training consultant, translation consultant, linguistics consultant, research/library, translation facilitator) without spouse names in URLs or titles. All have opaque or descriptive slugs.
needs_review.recommendation: Verify whether these represent true singletons (valid prospects), married couples with withheld spouse names (security withholding = needs_review), or single persons not raising personal support. Tier assessment depends on role verification and support-raising structure.

needs_review.finding: Mike Brooks marked retired Feb 29 2024 but appears on current partner pages as giving-URL prospect.
needs_review.evidence: Source https://www.wycliffe.org/partner/brooks shows "retired from Wycliffe Bible Translators on February 29, 2024, after serving 34 years."
needs_review.recommendation: Verify agency policy: are retired missionaries kept on giving URLs with donation redirects to a legacy/support fund (making them Tier B), or are they genuine prospects still raising personal support? Eve Brooks status unknown.

needs_review.issue: Hex ID confidence grading applies uniformly
needs_review.finding: 22 records carry opaque hex IDs (CEFDA0, 98E9B3, 8ECC77, 381CB5, 3DF2D8, 797465, ve85e1, 522542, 3ebb27, E5B4E7, EFCF8F, BB7514, 5CEF1A, 124E53, EAD359, 45D467, 93FEE8) and one UUID. Per brief, hex IDs are always medium confidence because the URL does not tie the page to the named person.
needs_review.evidence: Brief explicitly states: 'An opaque hex ID is medium, always... Do not grade these high.' Confirmed example: /partner/CEFDA0 is David & Fran Wakefield only because title says so; URL carries no name signal.
needs_review.recommendation: All 23 hex/UUID-keyed records emit as medium confidence. Do not upgrade to high despite clear names in titles or couples pages. These are mechanically sorted at ingest by ID tie strength.

needs_review.issue: Couples split on TITLE vs slug
needs_review.finding: All couples in this file were split based on their appearance in the page TITLE, not the slug. Slugs vary wildly (zakandlaura, moefamily, CEFDA0, 524542, etc.) but titles consistently name individuals and/or couples.
needs_review.evidence: Brief instructs: 'Split couples on the TITLE, not on the slug.' Example: /partner/CEFDA0 slug names neither David nor Fran, but title 'David & Fran Wakefield' names both, so both emit as separate records on the shared URL. This prevents emitting deceased spouses when agency quietly rewrites page.
needs_review.recommendation: Ingest process should verify all couple splits against reported title text. Any record where slug suggests couple (zakandlaura, bryan-lori-jones) but title shows only one person should emit only the titled person and route the unnamed to needs_review as potential deceased.
